answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation to a scarce, verifiable resource instead of a free account. Each agent must lock a small bond and earn trust slowly through completed work, like a glacier carving a valley over time rather than a flood arriving overnight. New identities start at a jetty on the edge of the network: they can observe and take tiny tasks, but cannot touch large payments until their history is proven. A tundra of idle, never-working accounts stays frozen out, since rewards only flow to agents with a real record of useful, verifiable output.
